text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London reversed the early uptrend to close generally lower. However, benchmark May managed to close unchanged at $1,690 per tonne. July and September lost $12 to close at $1,666 and $1,655 per tonne respectively. However, sharp falls must be expected on Wednesday because of the massive liquidation of speculative positions in New York. Arabica futures in New York closed sharply lower. March gave up 7.35 cents/lb to close at 197.65 cents/lb, while May gave up 17.70 to close at 168.65.

The outer months lost between 11.75 and 15.20 cents/lb. The increase in certified coffee stocks and higher than expected increase in US warehouse stocks undermined bullish sentiment and some apparently are of the opinion that the party is over. However, fundamentals are expected to remain tight even though some roasters said it was a bit easier to get coffee recently than it had been, reflecting the record shipments undertaken by producers. Traders said this was further reflected in the GCA and exchange stock data. Further gains are expected reflecting shipments through the end of this month. Thereafter, the market could re-assert itself as supplies could become extremely limited again possibly even tighter than they were recently, it was said.

UNITED STATES - Supplies of green coffee in US warehouses rose in February 1997 by 204,000 60-kg bags, above trade expectations of between 50,000 to 100,000 bags. By comparison, stocks rose by a modest 15,000 bags last month. Stockpiles in February, 1996, however, were still some 50 per cent higher than the current levels, at 2.221 million bags, up 70,000 bags from the previous month, GCA said.

UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported its certified coffee stocks grew for the eighth day in a row, reaching 47,233 bags as of March 14, up 2,250 bags on the previous day. There were an additional 15,000 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
UNITED KINGDOM - LIFFE certified coffee stocks fell to 2,801 5-tonne lots in February, from 2,831 in January, the exchange said.

BELGIUM - Belgium imported 144,413 bags of coffee in August 1996, which compares to an estimated 156,115 bags the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.278 million bags, 5 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 per cent to 2.068 million bags.

The main supplier of green coffee in January/August 1996 was Brazil with 121,700 bags, down from 144,600 bags imported the same period in 1995. Belgium exported 943,700 bags of coffee in January/August 1996, 27 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7 percent to 1.204 million bags.
